definitions.explanation: An informal second-person pronoun, typically used by men when addressing someone of equal or lower status.

examples.japanese: {君|きみ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{意見|いけん}→意見：01303_iken⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聞|き}かせて→聞く：00483_kiku⟧⟦ほしい→欲しい：01107_hoshii⟧。
examples.english: I want to hear your opinion.
If you say so, I'll go with you.

examples.japanese: {君|きみ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いない→いる：00495_iru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦みんな→みんな：02972_minna⟧⟦{寂|さび}しい→寂しい：00880_sabishii⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、⟦また→また：00969_mata⟧⟦{時間|じかん}→時間：00468_jikan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦{時|とき}→時：02918_toki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{遊|あそ}び→遊ぶ：00550_asobu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{来|き}て→来る：00254_kuru⟧⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧。
examples.english: We all miss you when you're not around, so come visit again when you have time.

notes:
{君|きみ} is an informal second-person pronoun used mainly by male speakers when addressing peers, subordinates, or close friends.

USAGE:
- Primarily used by men in casual settings
- Appropriate toward people of equal or lower social status
- Can sound condescending or rude if used toward a superior or stranger
- In romantic contexts (songs, poetry, intimate speech), it carries an affectionate tone
- Bosses sometimes use {君|きみ} toward younger employees
In Japanese, second-person pronouns are generally avoided when possible. Using someone's name + ⟦さん→〜さん：09848_san⟧ is usually more natural and polite than any pronoun.

OTHER SECOND-PERSON PRONOUNS:
- ⟦あなた→あなた：02565_anata⟧: polite/neutral, but avoided in casual male speech
- ⟦お{前|まえ}→お前：02533_omae⟧: very informal, can be rude or intimate
- ⟦あんた→あんた：27721_anta⟧: casual, slightly rough
